Descriptions of all Creepy Dice items below.
All Creepy Dice can be canceled out if the player under its effect uses a Mushroom, Double Dice, Triple Dice, or Custom Dice Block.
**Creepy Dice Block**- Use on a player to make it so their die can only roll a number from 1 to 3. Costs 3 coins (or 1 coin at One-Coin Shop).
**Creepy Dice Block Tickets**- Bargain tickets to use Creepy Dice Blocks, which roll a number from 1 to 3, two to four times. Costs 5 coins.
Of note is that you are capable of targeting yourself with Creepy Dice Blocks too (whether the single or ticket). If for some reason you want to roll low and maybe don't have a Custom Dice Block to get exactly what you want.
**Super Creepy Dice**- Use on all opponents to make it so their Dice can only roll a number from 1 to 3. Costs 5 coins.
Unlike the regular creepy dice and the tickets, you can't target yourself with the super creepy dice. That said, it targets all opponents instead.
Do you use creepy dice? And if so, which ones are your favorite?
Do not collect junk in your hearts. You can make yourself happy if you don't let others make you unhappy.
- Fredrik Backman, "The Answer is No" p57

**Cozy****(Topic Creator)5 months ago#2
On my end, I rarely use them. If I do, it's going to be the Super Creepies; affecting 3 opponents is the appeal there.
Still easily countered via a lot of common items, but my thought process with using super creepy dice is when opponents also have things like Plunder Chests, Warp Boxes, Shop Hop Boxes, Swap Mirrors, etc. Particularly if they could also end up near traps if they use those items instead, and risk rolling lower numbers.
Those aren't situations that happen often though, so still I think Creepies tend to be fairly niche. Even the supers.
Do not collect junk in your hearts. You can make yourself happy if you don't let others make you unhappy.
- Fredrik Backman, "The Answer is No" p57
(edited5 months ago)

**ShyRanger****4 months ago#3
Creepy Dice and Super Creepy Dice are amazing when someone has a buddy. If an opponent has one you can basically make them waste a turn with a low roll. If you have a buddy, then the Super Creepy is good for building further distance between you and your opponents.
However the Double Dice can also take care of both of these situations and is usually more convenient to get. So creepy is okay but outclassed.
I think the best way to make it perfectly good would be to make it uncancellable with other items like Mushrooms, basically force it on someone no matter what. But overall it's good if in the right situation and you don't have other stuff.

# Creepy Dice Block Tickets

| Creepy Dice Block Tickets | |
| --- | --- |
| | |
| Description | |
| Bargain tickets to use Creepy Dice, which roll a number from 1 to 3, two to four times. | |
| Appears in | Super Mario Party Jamboree (2024) |
| Effect | Allows the player to use Creepy Dice Blocks 2-4 times. |
| Related Creepy Dice Block | |

The Creepy Dice Block Tickets are an item in Super Mario Party Jamboree. They consist of two to four individual tickets, with the number of tickets being random, allowing the player to use a Creepy Dice Block (on themself or other players) two, three, or four times before they are all used up. 

Creepy Dice Block Tickets are usually found in Kamek's Item Shops, where they cost five coins. They can be obtained on Roll 'em Raceway before the shop inventory is updated or on Mario's Rainbow Castle after the shop inventory is updated. Outside of that, they can also appear in an Item Bag.

The Mushroom Tickets are an item in Super Mario Party Jamboree. They consist of two to four individual tickets, with the number of tickets being random, allowing the player to use a Mushroom two, three, or four times before they are all used up. The player can only use the tickets on themself. 

One set of Mushroom Tickets costs six coins. They can be obtained at Item Shops at Roll 'em Raceway, Mario's Rainbow Castle, Goomba Lagoon with a Pro Rules ruleset, and Western Land, or they can be received on a Lucky Space or an Item Space. On boards where Mushroom Tickets are normally not obtainable, they can also appear in an Item Bag.

# Turbo Dice

| Turbo Dice | |
| --- | --- |
| | |
| Description | |
| Roll 4 dice and move at high speed! Will only stop for crossroads. | |
| First appearance | Super Mario Party Jamboree (2024) |
| Latest appearance | Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV (2025) |
| Effect | Allows the player to roll four Dice Blocks, at the cost of skipping board events. (Super Mario Party Jamboree) |

The Turbo Dice is a special Dice Block in the Mario Party series introduced in Super Mario Party Jamboree. 

The Turbo Dice only appears on the board Roll 'em Raceway. It allows the player to roll four Dice Blocks, granting four to 40 spaces of movement. However, this causes the player to skip any board events they cross, including the Star Space. They are still allowed to choose which direction to go to at junctions. It costs 12 coins at the Koopa Troopa Shop, and is one of the dice items that can be randomly obtained from paying 10 coins at the Dice Shop pit stop. When used, the user's kart gains gold tires and shoots fire from its exhaust pipes.

# Dominate the Minigames! Super Mario Party Jamboree Tips - Play Nintendo
URL: https://play.nintendo.com/news-tips/tips-tricks/super-mario-party-jamboree-tips-and-tricks/

Dominate the Minigames! Super Mario Party Jamboree Tips - Play Nintendo

Skip to main contentSkip to News & Tips navigation

The competition can be fierce in the Super Mario Party Jamboree game for the Nintendo Switch system. Here are a few tips and tricks that might come in handy for when you want to cause a little chaos among your opponents!

### You can steal stuff

And by “stuff,” we mean stuff in the game. You can grow your coin collection by stealing them from other players. You can even steal another player’s Jamboree Buddy!

### You can mess with your opponents

Each game board includes an exclusive item that can throw a wrench into another player’s plans. On the Gooma Lagoon board, for example, you could use the Tide Shell to block your opponent’s path with the help of the rising tide. So sneaky!

### You can go turbo

On the Roll ‘em Raceway game board, you can use the board-exclusive Turbo Dice item to roll four Dice Blocks at once. That means you can run laps around the players and zoom to the Star before anyone else.

### You can steal more stuff

The player with the most Stars at the end of the game wins. And guess what? You can steal some of these celestial wonders from your opponents with the help of Boo!

### You can strategize

Some players just roll the Dice Block and leave the rest to fate. But you can have a plan, like using all of your items in a single turn and totally blowing past the competition.

ESRB Rating: Everyone with Mild Fantasy Violence
